Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: high resolution 2D action-game sprite strip.
Input reference: character identity and exact outfit reference, NOT a composition to reuse. Exactly the mature bearded man in this reference: black high ponytail with red tie, red lamellar breastplate, black sleeves and trousers, red-and-gold floral cloak, red shin armor and black/gold shoes. Keep his robust compact six-head-tall game proportions and face. ONLY this man.
Draw ONE complete continuous action sequence: Second light sword strike: reverse rising diagonal cut from low rear left to high forward right.
Exactly TWELVE full-body consecutive drawings, arranged in EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and THREE ROWS, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Canvas 1536x1536 square. Each invisible cell is 384x512. Groundline near cell bottom, same camera, same scale in EVERY cell. Human skull-to-soles height approximately 330 pixels at upright stance; consistently large highly detailed native drawings, NOT enlarged little sprites. Leave generous clear margins and 30+ pixels between ALL neighboring figures and weapons. Weapon fits wholly within each own cell; no neighboring contact. Character primarily faces right, three-quarter side view like reference.
Timing: frames 1 through 6 are SIX separately drawn gradual anticipation stages; frame 7 (row 2 column 3) is maximum extended IMPACT toward right; frames 8-10 gradually follow through; frames 11-12 progressively return to the SAME ready stance. Distinct feet, knees, hips, torso, shoulders, elbows, wrists and weapon pose at every stage. Freezeable precise still drawings. Frame 1 and frame 12 have same human size and appearance as reference standing.
Style: exactly reference's crisp hand-painted arcade ink and cel shading. Sharp closed ink contours, solid opaque colors with very thin antialiased edges, detailed face, armor plates and cloth hems. NO motion blur, soft blur, fog, glow, smears, ghosting, transparent trails, speedlines, weapon trail, ground shadow, text, borders, grid or detached effects. No model change or chibi change between frames. Genuine transparent background, full clean alpha. No backdrop.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: high resolution game consecutive sprite frames.
Reference defines the ONLY character: mature bearded Nobunaga in black high ponytail/red tie, bright red lamellar armor, black trousers, red and gold flower cloak, same face and compact robust body proportions. NO colored backdrop from reference.
Draw SIX sequential full-body poses in TWO COLUMNS and THREE ROWS on a square canvas. Two WIDE cells per row, 50px clear outer margins and a 50px empty center gutter. Body skull-to-soles height 270px, fixed consistent scale. Entire blade and cape stay inside its own wide cell. Sharp ink and cel shading like reference.
Action: third light attack, a full-body pivot and broad horizontal sword slash toward the RIGHT. This is the FIRST half, global frames 0-5, ONLY progressive anticipation: 0 ready sword forward at waist, 1 hips begin pivot left, 2 shoulder drawn back, 3 rear-view torso with sword drawn across chest, 4 coil deeper and lift lead heel, 5 maximum coiled wind-up with sword pointing backward, immediately before impact. SIX DIFFERENT poses, not duplicated images. Full feet with real weight shifts. No motion blur, no weapon trails, no ghosting, no floating pixels, no dust, no glows, no shadows, no text or lines. Genuinely transparent background. No overlapping figures, NO CROPPED BLADES.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep the SAME six full-body Nobunaga drawings, same clothes, face, proportions, two-column three-row transparent sprite sheet, and same sequential sword poses. Correct ONLY these defects: the first two drawings each have an EXTRA third hand resting at the waist. REMOVE that spare waist hand; each man has EXACTLY TWO hands and TWO arms, both hands gripping the sword handle beside his right shoulder. All six blade tips, cape edges and feet must be fully visible with minimum 30 pixels transparent margin at the outside and 20 pixel gap between rows. The upper-left blade is cut by the top edge: reposition that complete figure down and right slightly or lower his raised weapon slightly to keep its entire tip inside, preserving its body scale. Neighboring figures must not touch. Same crisp opaque line art, no blur, no new background, no effects. Preserve genuine transparent alpha.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: crisp high-resolution 2D game consecutive sprite sheet.
Reference is IDENTITY and OUTFIT ONLY, not poses to copy. Exactly the same mature bearded Nobunaga: black high ponytail/red tie, bright red lamellar armor, black trousers, red-and-gold floral cloak, red shin armor, black/gold shoes; stocky compact six-head proportions, same head/hand/leg sizes. Reference brown background must NOT be drawn.
Draw SIX genuinely different consecutive full-body drawings in exactly TWO COLUMNS and THREE ROWS. Square canvas. Each wide cell has full blade/cape/feet inside it, minimum 30 pixels gap between adjacent opaque shapes; clear outer margins. Large native anatomical drawings, upright skull-to-soles approximately 300 pixels at actual output, NEVER shrink body to fit a long sword; instead sword can sweep in the wide cell. Consistent anatomical scale across all six frames, same camera facing right. TWO hands grip the single sword handle in EVERY frame, right hand near guard and left hand near pommel.
Sharp closed ink outlines, opaque cel colors, detailed armor and face, no blur/soft edges, no motion smears/trails/ghosts, no text/grid/borders, no shadows, no background, true alpha transparency.
Motion is a game adaptation of armored Japanese two-handed sword cuts. Hips and foot pressure lead shoulders; bent elbows carry blade through an ARC. A CUT passes in front then finishes on the OPPOSITE side. NEVER substitute both straight arms thrusting sword point horizontally forward. End weapon direction must match the stated pose. Do not draw all frames holding sword forward.

Action light1, SECOND half (impact through follow-through and recovery). Global sequence has twelve drawings, frame 6 is contact. Draw ONLY these six global frames in row-major order:
6: IMPACT: descending diagonal kesagiri cut through space in front of torso; hilt near sternum, blade angles down-right, BOTH elbows bent, not a straight-arm thrust.
7: Continue the same diagonal arc through lower front; shoulders turn past target, wrists guide edge through.
8: Finish across the OPPOSITE LEFT hip: both hands at left waist, blade tip points down-left behind body, chest has rotated through.
9: Hold balanced low opposite-side finish briefly, front knee flexed, trailing heel lifted.
10: Withdraw hands close to waist and relax shoulders into ready.
11: Ready guard returns, same size, sword low forward, elbows relaxed.

Action heavy2, FIRST half (preparation into cutting). Global sequence has twelve drawings, frame 6 is contact. Draw ONLY these six global frames in row-major order:
0: Waki guard: BOTH hands near RIGHT rear waist, blade hidden trailing back to screen-left, point low behind body.
1: Bend knees, transfer weight onto rear leg, hands remain tucked at rear right waist.
2: Coil hips and shoulders away from opponent, blade nearly horizontal behind hips.
3: Maximum waist-side coil, back three-quarter view, tip points backward-left, hands close to right hip.
4: Step toward target, front heel lands, pelvis starts rotation; hands lead blade around right flank.
5: Blade arcs around waist into front, BOTH elbows remain flexed; shoulders catch up with hips.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Preserve this exact six-drawing Nobunaga sequence and its two-column three-row layout, identity, scale, face, cape, legs and sword blade direction. In the MIDDLE LEFT drawing (row 2 column 1, global frame 8), change only the arms and sword grip: BOTH HANDS must hold the SAME sword hilt beside the left hip. The free right hand at the other side of the waist must move across to the hilt beside the gripping hand. TWO hands on one hilt, elbows bent, blade remains pointing BACKWARD-LEFT after sweeping across the body. No third arm or hand. Every other pose stays unchanged. Entire swords/capes/feet inside canvas, transparent outside, same sharp opaque ink and cel colors, no blur/effects/shadows.

This reference shows the already finished first half of a lateral sword slash. Continue its last coiled pose, same character and anatomical scale. Draw ONLY final six global frames in row-major order:
6 IMPACT: both hands sweep close to navel, sword cutting edge travels sideways across front; blade angled diagonally forward-down, BOTH elbows bent. Front foot steps, hips rotate. Do NOT draw an extended forward thrust.
7 Continue the very same sweeping arc; hands move from center to left waist, tip turns around with body, chest rotated farther.
8 Follow-through crosses to OPPOSITE LEFT side; both hands at left hip, blade extends down-left BEHIND body, shoulders turned through.
9 Low opposite-side finish, tip still down-left, knees absorb weight shift.
10 Unwind shoulders and return hilt close to center waist.
11 Original relaxed waist-level ready stance, same head and body size as first reference frame. Do not repeat the same pose.
